raw_segments.text: Lear, oh, reason not the need.
Our basest beggars are in the poorest thing superfluous.
Allow not nature more than nature needs, man's life is cheap as beasts.
Thou art a lady.
If only to go warm were gorgeous, why nature needs not what thou gorgeous wears to you
which scarcely keeps thee warm.
But for true need, you heavens, give me that patience, patience I need.
You see me here, you gods, a poor old man, as full of grief as age, wretched in both.
If it be you that stirs these daughters' hearts against their father, fool me not so
much to bear it tamely.
Touch me with noble anger and let not women's weapons, water drops, stain my man's cheeks.
No you unnatural hags, I will have such revenges on you both that all the world shall.
I will do such things.
What they are yet I know not, but they shall be the terrors of the earth.
You think I'll weep?
No, I'll not weep.
Storm and tempest.
I have full cause of weeping, but this heart shall break into a hundred thousand flaws
or air I'll weep.
O fool, I shall go mad.
